entradas.text: I arrived at the Ministry of Defense and entered the War Room to discuss the war plans with the general staff.
I had never seen this room so packed with people. Every single top-ranking general and admiral in Sordland was in attendance.
"Very well."
"Cut the chatter and let's start."
entradas.menu: "Cut the chatter and let's start."

entradas.text: "Mr. President."
In addition to the military officers, their assistants were spread out around the room. They stopped their chatter immediately and saluted me.
"At ease, gentlemen."
entradas.menu: "At ease, gentlemen."

entradas.text: I saluted.
entradas.menu: Salute.

entradas.text: "Please do."
entradas.menu: "Please do."

entradas.text: I gestured for him to start.
entradas.menu: Gesture for him to start.

entradas.text: The generals sat down and I took my seat at the head of the table.
I took a look around. After my order to purge the general staff, I couldn't recognise many of the faces. These generals were certainly younger than their predecessors.
The room immediately went quiet. Everyone had their attention on Iosef. He turned to me.
Iosef was standing over the table, arranging tokens atop an oversized map of Sordland and Rumburg. He walked up to me and saluted.
"Silence!"
"Mr. President. May I begin?"
Iosef stood up and picked up an extendable pointer from a shelf on the wall.
I took a look around. General Valken nodded at me.
The chattering among the staff began again. Iosef extended the pointer and loudly hit the map on the table right in its center.
"Everyone in this room has read the reports that the Queen of Rumburg is getting ready for a nationwide speech in two weeks."
"We have credible intel that she will be announcing a declaration of war against Sordland."
"The time has come."
"Mr. President, at this point we are sure that they are preparing for a large-scale invasion."
"The Rumburgian troop movements in the last 24 hours indicate that they are bolstering their frontline strength."
"The time has come."
"Gentlemen, the day of retribution is upon us."
"It is high time we put an end to the wretched nation of Rumburg."
"I am announcing 'Operation Fallen Crown'."
"The main intent of this operation is simple."
"The complete capitulation of Rumburg."
As Iosef was speaking, assistants handed out small booklets detailing the operation.
"I have faith in our soldiers. We will persevere."
entradas.menu: "I have faith in our soldiers. We will persevere."

entradas.text: "Unfortunately faith does not win wars."
"How soon will they commence the attack?"
entradas.menu: "How soon will they commence the attack?"

entradas.text: "How does our military strength compare to theirs?"
entradas.menu: "How does our military strength compare to theirs?"

entradas.text: "Give it to me straight. What are the odds of success?"
entradas.menu: "Give it to me straight. What are the odds of success?"

entradas.text: "Judging from their movements and the insider information we have received..."
"We have two, maybe three weeks if we're lucky."
There was a collective gasp from some of the generals' assistants.
"The 6th army is currently garrisoned at Narbel, awaiting orders."
"The estimates put their active military personnel at around 900,000 to one million. Meanwhile, we have approximately 600,000 soldiers on the ground."
"If we played our cards right, I would comfortably say the odds were high."
"The 2nd army is standing by at Laren for a possible assault from the north."
"To answer your question, I don't know. But I will do everything I can to ensure our victory. Even if it costs me my life."
"But we didn't play our cards right, did we?"
"We currently have the 1st Army deployed at Estord to reinforce the border. This is the place they will most likely attack from."
"I repeatedly warned you that the decisions your administration was making would weaken our military."
"We will make them regret they ever crossed us, that's what we are going to do."
"Hah. Odds of success?"
"Let's begin with our land forces."
"Let me tell you something, Mr. President."
"Rumburg doesn't have any idea what or who they are dealing with."
Some of the generals laughed.
Iosef glanced over at the generals and stopped at Valken. He shook his head.
Iosef glanced over at the generals and they all nodded in agreement.
"We have approximately 410 planes, of which 140 are state-of-the-art jets."
"We have 600 ready to go and another 100 in reserve."
"To say that I am worried would be an understatement."
entradas.menu: "To say that I am worried would be an understatement."

entradas.text: "The Queen seems set on making an enemy of us."
entradas.menu: "The Queen seems set on making an enemy of us."

entradas.text: "She is out for blood, that's for sure. They think they will emerge victorious."
"Meanwhile, Rumburg has around 110 ships -- and according to our latest intelligence reports, high-tech submarines as well."
"That's why we have gathered here today. To discuss what we are going to do."
"I understand the situation."
entradas.menu: "I understand the situation."

entradas.text: "Overall, their numbers may seem superior, but I would like to remind everyone that wars are not won with numbers alone."
"We will destroy their armies and send them back to whatever hellhole they came from."
"But soldiers with faith do, Iosef."
"And look at where we are now. Exactly the situation that I foresaw."
"Then let's prove her wrong."
"Good. Now we have to talk about our defensive strategy."
"Our fleet currently totals up to 80 ships with the new destroyers and battleships, as well as about 100.000 sailors."
"Rest assured, Mr. President. I am more than confident that we will win."
"Our fleet currently totals up to 60 ships and approximately 60,000 sailors."
"How soon do we plan to start the offensive?"
entradas.menu: "How soon do we plan to start the offensive?"

entradas.text: "That depends on the decisions we make today."
"Since we are about to declare war on them, I recommend we hit them hard with the element of surprise before they can organize their troops."
"Unfortunately, they will have to take a side role in this war since the main theatre will be on land."
"Fortunately, the main theatre of this war will be on land, so their navy will have a limited impact."
"With that said, if we use them wisely, I believe they could have a significant impact."
"I predict that they will try to block our seaports, reducing our trade and disrupting our supplies."
"Regrettably, we don't have an estimate on how many submarines they have. "
"Regardless, they are prepared to fight and die for their country, Mr. President."
"Unfortunately our combat readiness has been getting worse and worse over the years. That's because we did not allocate enough budget to hold proper drills."
"Now I see why you wanted that budget so badly."
entradas.menu: "Now I see why you wanted that budget so badly."

entradas.text: "It's too late now. War is at our doorstep."
"There is something else I wanted to mention, Mr. President."
"Due to the potential of an invasion, all three armies have been undergoing rigorous drills, especially during the past few months."
"They are prepared to fight and die for their country, Mr. President."
"Good. That gives me some confidence at least."
entradas.menu: "Good. That gives me some confidence at least."

entradas.text: "You have done well, generals."
entradas.menu: "You have done well, generals."

entradas.text: "Will it be enough?"
entradas.menu: "Will it be enough?"

entradas.text: "It must be."
"No need for flattery. Just doing our duty."
"Due to the potential of an invasion, all three armies have been undergoing rigorous drills, especially during the past few months."
"Good to hear."
"Your son Franc is currently deployed at the Rumburg border. He is serving in the 1st Army as an Officer Cadet."
The entire room turned to me to hear what I would say.
"They are prepared to fight and die for their country, Mr. President."
"But no worries, Mr. President. I'm sure he will be fine."
"Regardless, they are prepared to fight and die for their country, Mr. President."
"The Sordland military code is clear. He will serve his country just like everyone else."
"Unfortunately our combat readiness has been getting worse and worse over the years. That's because we did not allocate enough budget to hold proper drills."
"Your son Franc is currently deployed at the Rumburg border. He is serving in the 1st Army as a Private First Class."
"No worries, Mr. President."
"Pull him back to Holsord immediately. That's an order."
entradas.menu: "Pull him back to Holsord immediately. That's an order."

entradas.text: "Right away, Mr. President."
"I'm getting more and more worried."
entradas.menu: "I'm getting more and more worried."

entradas.text: "I'm just telling it to you as it is."
"Thank you for letting me know, Iosef."
entradas.menu: "Thank you for letting me know, Iosef."

entradas.text: "I'm afraid I can't do that. Even if it's an order from you."
"I thought you should know."
"Now, let's start discussing our path to victory in this war."
"Our top strategic location is Thornbourgh."
"Tzarsbourgh is the intersection of Rumburg's complex railway system. If we take it, we'll have more options on both the offensive and defensive."
"Another strategic location is Dome. Capturing Dome will prevent us from being surrounded and cut off from the east."
"Our top strategic location is Thornbourgh."
"Rumburg's capital and the Queen's residence."
"Needless to say, if we manage to capture the queen, the war will end."
"It will also reduce the battle line we have to cover with our limited numbers."
"Tzarsbourgh is the intersection of Rumburg's complex railway system. If we take it, we'll have more options on both the offensive and defensive."
"Rumburg's capital and the Queen's residence."
"Needless to say, if we manage to capture the queen, the war will end."
"What if she flees Thornbourgh before we get there?"
entradas.menu: "What if she flees Thornbourgh before we get there?"

entradas.text: "I am a proud soldier of Sordland, Mr. President. I'd rather die than give up Holsord to invaders."
"And I know a prideful person when I see one. If we strike fast, we can capture the capital and the queen before she comes to her senses."
"What are the chances of capturing their capital?"
entradas.menu: "What are the chances of capturing their capital?"

entradas.text: "There might be an opportunity to push for Thornbourgh after we capture Tzarsbourgh."
"But we are ahead of ourselves. We'll get to that when we discuss the war plan."
"Can we still win without capturing Thornbourgh?"
entradas.menu: "Can we still win without capturing Thornbourgh?"

entradas.text: "If we can't do that, it will become a war of attrition. Whether we can outlast them depends on our economy."
"Let's move on. What are the other objectives?"
entradas.menu: "Let's move on. What are the other objectives?"

entradas.text: "Aside from Thornbourgh, the location that we must capture to even have a chance to win this war is Tzarsbourgh."
"It will also reduce the battle line we have to cover with our limited numbers."
"I will be frank. We can't fend them off alone. We need help."
"We need to do whatever we can by ourselves. I know we can win."
entradas.menu: "We need to do whatever we can by ourselves. I know we can win."

entradas.text: "Thankfully, we have allies. We must call them to war in order to win."
"That is true, but.."
"Other than that, we do have allies that could aid us but I see no point."
"We can fend them off easily."
"At any rate, this is what we are dealing with."
"I will be frank. We can't fend them off alone. We need help."
"We are all alone in this war."
"Very well. Call our allies to the war."
entradas.menu: "Very well. Call our allies to the war."

entradas.text: "No. We don't need anyone else to defend our borders."
entradas.menu: "No. We don't need anyone else to defend our borders."

entradas.text: "You are talking about fighting against a million men. A million!"
"We are now a full member of CSP and they will join us in the war, which will be of tremendous support."
"You tasked us with the defense of this nation, and we will defend our nation."
"Mr. President. I must insist. We are the experts. Please listen to us. Otherwise we will lose this war."
"Your confidence is inspiring, Mr. President."
"We will call our allies to the war."
"With the power of ATO behind us, Rumburg has absolutely no chance."
"We have begun communications already. Now we can make it official."
"Here is the hard truth."
"You dare defy my orders?"
entradas.menu: "You dare defy my orders?"

entradas.text: "Very well. I will trust your judgement."
entradas.menu: "Very well. I will trust your judgement."

entradas.text: "Well said, Mr. President."
"Thank you, Mr. President."
"Mr. President. I have a duty to this nation to protect it from its enemies."
"We are now a full member of ATO and they will join us in the war, which will be of tremendous support."
"Even if that means defying you."
"With the power of CSP behind us, Rumburg has absolutely no chance."
"Please let me continue."
Seeing no support from the generals around me, I had to sit down.
"Thank you, Mr. President."
"It is our war to fight. We will not depend on others."
entradas.menu: "It is our war to fight. We will not depend on others."

entradas.text: "You are talking about fighting against a million men. A million!"
"Sordland will stand alone as always."
"This is preposterous."
"Hah. We don't need anyone else to protect our country."
Iosef let out a deep sigh.
"Then we will have to plan accordingly."
"Very well. We don't need anyone else to defend our borders."
entradas.menu: "Very well. We don't need anyone else to defend our borders."

entradas.text: "We can't risk anything. Call our allies to the war."
entradas.menu: "We can't risk anything. Call our allies to the war."

entradas.text: "I assure you, we can defend our borders just fine without further help."
"Maybe we should've tried to get some allies after all."
entradas.menu: "Maybe we should've tried to get some allies after all."

entradas.text: "Sordland has always been alone, Iosef."
entradas.menu: "Sordland has always been alone, Iosef."

entradas.text: "Very well. I will trust your judgement then."
entradas.menu: "Very well. I will trust your judgement then."

entradas.text: "We do have allies that could aid us, but I see no point."
"I know, but this might help our image on the world stage."
entradas.menu: "I know, but this might help our image on the world stage."

entradas.text: "Hmm. Very well then."
"I said I don't want to take any risks. We will call our allies."
entradas.menu: "I said I don't want to take any risks. We will call our allies."

entradas.text: "That's ridiculous. We can't fend them off alone. We need help."
"No. We *had* to."
"We can fend them off easily."
Before Iosef could continue, a soldier walked in and handed him a note.
"Mr. President."
"He's not authorized to join this meeting. Let's proceed."
entradas.menu: "He's not authorized to join this meeting. Let's proceed."

entradas.text: "Mr. President, Deivid Wisci has requested to join the war planning session."
"Tell him he is not needed here."
entradas.menu: "Tell him he is not needed here."

entradas.text: "Let him in."
entradas.menu: "Let him in."

entradas.text: After the soldier left the room, Devid slowly walked in. He fired off a round of salutes to the generals, then approached me.
"As you wish."
"As you wish."
"What are you doing here, my friend?"
entradas.menu: "What are you doing here, my friend?"

entradas.text: "So you're not retiring after all?"
entradas.menu: "So you're not retiring after all?"

entradas.text: "What do you want?"
entradas.menu: "What do you want?"

entradas.text: "Anton, please allow me to assist in the war plans."
"Deivid, you are a diplomat, not a general."
entradas.menu: "Deivid, you are a diplomat, not a general."

entradas.text: "What kind of guidance are you talking about?"
entradas.menu: "What kind of guidance are you talking about?"

entradas.text: "Do you think our generals here lack the know-how to win us this war?"
entradas.menu: "Do you think our generals here lack the know-how to win us this war?"

entradas.text: "Of course I lack the military knowledge of our esteemed generals. But I do know people, Mr. President."
Iosef and the other generals fixed him with a sharp look.
Iosef and Valken fixed him with a sharp look.
"Especially our own people. And our allies."
"Deivid, you worry too much. We have no need to involve allies in this war."
entradas.menu: "Deivid, you worry too much. We have no need to involve allies in this war."

entradas.text: "Why? Our allies love us!"
entradas.menu: "Why? Our allies love us!"

entradas.text: Deivid stood there and stared at me for a moment.
"Anton, are you serious? The independence of our republic is at risk."
"General Valken assured me that our allies are not needed in this war."
entradas.menu: "General Valken assured me that our allies are not needed in this war."

entradas.text: "I hope you'll reconsider. Even if we somehow win the war alone, it will devastate our economy."
"Having allies present will lessen the burden on both our soldiers and our people."
"Precisely! We cannot place our republic in the hands of foreign interests."
"We need to show the world that Sordland can stand on its own two feet."
"Sorry, Wisci. I tried to advise them, but to no avail. This... This is madness."
"Sorry, Wisci. I tried to advise them, but to no avail. This is madness."
"You are underestimating the power of the Sordish armed forces. We can win this war by ourselves."
entradas.menu: "You are underestimating the power of the Sordish armed forces. We can win this war by ourselves."

entradas.text: "Mr. President, please reconsider."
"Deivid, you're right as usual. Even if we could win the war alone, the cost would be too high. We need help."
entradas.menu: "Deivid, you're right as usual. Even if we could win the war alone, the cost would be too high. We need help."

entradas.text: "Thank you, Anton."
"No, my decision is final."
entradas.menu: "No, my decision is final."

entradas.text: "Deivid, you can leave now."
entradas.menu: "Deivid, you can leave now."

entradas.text: "It seems that I was wrong. I am of no use here."
Deivid let our a heavy sigh.
"Sorry to disturb you, Mr. President."
"What allies? You've gone to all this trouble for nothing, Deivid."
entradas.menu: "What allies? You've gone to all this trouble for nothing, Deivid."

entradas.text: "Allies? Who needs them? We have full trust in our capacity to win this war by ourselves."
entradas.menu: "Allies? Who needs them? We have full trust in our capacity to win this war by ourselves."

entradas.text: "You might be right about that."
entradas.menu: "You might be right about that."

entradas.text: "You're afraid that they might backstab us?"
entradas.menu: "You're afraid that they might backstab us?"

entradas.text: "No, they wouldn't dare. The international repercussions would be far too high."
"I'm sure that our allies will agree to fight by our side."
"Glad you've finally come to your senses, Mr. President."
"Ridiculous. You'd rather trust this ancient diplomat than your highest-ranking general in a time of war."
"The decision is made, Valken. Let's move on."
"Beneficial though our foreign partners may be, I would still advise you to keep a close eye on them."
"First you beg me to call them in, now you're suspicious of them?"
entradas.menu: "First you beg me to call them in, now you're suspicious of them?"

entradas.text: "Don't get me wrong, Mr. President. The point I made still stands."
Deivid gracefully motioned for Iosef to step aside. He was now at the head of the table.
"However, depending on our plans and our past interactions with them, some may be more committed than others."
"He has a point, Mr. President. It's worth keeping that in mind."
"This is exactly why we shouldn't involve them."
"I assure you I am, Mr. President. But your term has not ended yet, and you could clearly still use my guidance."
Deivid turned around and left the room.
"Let us move on to our war strategy."
"Our first objective is taking Tzarsbourgh."
"There are three options on the table at the moment."
"I thought Rumburg was hard to invade."
entradas.menu: "I thought Rumburg was hard to invade."

entradas.text: "Can't we just defend our border?"
entradas.menu: "Can't we just defend our border?"

entradas.text: "What are the plans to take Tzarsbourgh?"
entradas.menu: "What are the plans to take Tzarsbourgh?"

entradas.text: "So how are we taking this city?"
entradas.menu: "So how are we taking this city?"

entradas.text: "Do continue, General."
entradas.menu: "Do continue, General."

entradas.text: "Unfortunately, Mr. President, simple defense is not a possibility."
"Entering a war of attrition without dealing a killing blow to Rumburg will place us in a disastrous position."
"They will simply wear us out with their larger military and superior technology."
"Entering a war of attrition without dealing a killing blow to Rumburg will place us in a disastrous position."
"They will simply wear us out with their larger military and superior technology."
"If we only defend, the world will see this war as a stalemate."
"Especially when we have ATO on our side."
"If we only defend, the world will see this war as a stalemate."
"Especially when we have ATO on our side."
"With the CSP looming on the horizon, looking for an excuse to intervene..."
"I believe we should strike as fast as we can. If they see that Rumburg is a lost cause, they might not join the war."
"Especially when we have CSP on our side."
"If we only defend, the world will see this war as a stalemate."
"If we only defend, the world will see this war as a stalemate."
"Especially when we have CSP on our side."
"With the CSP looming on the horizon, looking for an excuse to intervene..."
"I believe we should strike as fast as we can. If they see that Rumburg is a lost cause, they might not join the war."
"However, if we take two of their key cities, we might be able to turn the tide on them."
"Furthermore, these will give us leverage once the peace negotiations begin."
"The best defense is certainly a good offense."
entradas.menu: "The best defense is certainly a good offense."

entradas.text: I heard the sound of boots running down the hall. A soldier rushed in, urgently pulled Valken aside and whispered in his ear.
The general's face turned white. He hurriedly straightened the lapels on his uniform.
"Mr. President, it seems we will be joined by a very esteemed guest today."
"Who is it?"
entradas.menu: "Who is it?"

entradas.text: "Another general? I thought everyone was here."
entradas.menu: "Another general? I thought everyone was here."

entradas.text: "Must be someone important to make you react like that."
entradas.menu: "Must be someone important to make you react like that."

entradas.text: "Colonel."
"It is an honor to have you here at this time of need, sir."
Before Valken could answer, the door swung open. Every single man in the room immediately stood bolt upright and saluted.
Tarquin Soll was dressed in his old uniform, the insignia of the 6th Army of the Sordish Armed Forces displayed prominently on his chest.
"Gentlemen."
"How can these old bones of mine rest while my beloved country goes to war?"
"What are you doing here?"
entradas.menu: "What are you doing here?"

entradas.text: "It is indeed an honor, sir."
entradas.menu: "It is indeed an honor, sir."

entradas.text: "Got bored of your gardening, old man?"
entradas.menu: "Got bored of your gardening, old man?"

entradas.text: I raised my hand in salute.
entradas.menu: Salute him.

entradas.text: "Show some respect, Mr. President."
"There is no greater honor than to protect one's nation, Mr. President."
"I'm here to show you how to win this war, son."
Soll gave a satisfactory nod.
"I don't think the Colonel's war credentials need to be reiterated."
"Having him here will be of immense help to us. As well as a morale booster for our troops."
"I may not be as fit as I was during my last war, but I still remember how the game is played."
"Colonel, you're too humble."
"He has no right to be here."
entradas.menu: "He has no right to be here."

entradas.text: "With your help, this war is already won."
entradas.menu: "With your help, this war is already won."

entradas.text: "You've meddled in my business for the last time. Guards!"
entradas.menu: "You've meddled in my business for the last time. Guards!"

entradas.text: "I'm looking forward to working with you, Colonel."
entradas.menu: "I'm looking forward to working with you, Colonel."

entradas.text: "Are you saying the founder of this republic has no right to come to its aid at a critical juncture?"
"Mr. President, with all due respect, the Colonel is here and he shall stay as long as he wishes."
Nobody in the room moved a muscle.
"Not yet, my boy. Shall we get started?"
"So am I, Mr. President. You have shown great leadership in times of peace. Let us see how you act in times of war."
"Shall we get started?"
"Certainly, sir."
"They will simply wear us out with their larger military and superior technology."
"However, if we take two of their key cities, we might be able to turn the tide on them."
"One is to simply dig in and endure their first wave of attack, then retaliate after they are weakened."
"Our first option is to launch a large full-scale offensive. Which I don't recommend since it will probably end in a complete massacre of our troops."
"Our second option is to launch a full-scale offensive on Tzarsbourgh. We will strike at them hard and fast before they have the chance to draw first blood."
"Which is insane in my opinion."
"Our second option is to do a pincer attack to wipe out their forces and then march toward Tzarsbourgh."
"How is digging in and waiting for them to attack a good option?"
entradas.menu: "How is digging in and waiting for them to attack a good option?"

entradas.text: "Why can't we just launch an assault on Tzarsbourgh?"
entradas.menu: "Why can't we just launch an assault on Tzarsbourgh?"

entradas.text: "Tell me more about the pincer attack."
entradas.menu: "Tell me more about the pincer attack."

entradas.text: "Which makes no sense."
"You're handing them the time and motivation to come up with a plan to attack us."
"The border fortifications we built are for this very purpose."
"We don't even have the manpower to cover the entire border."
"The expansion of our land forces will serve to fill any gap we have in our border."
"They outnumbered us, Iosef. With this move we will destroy or, at worst, limit the effectiveness of their advantage."
"There are two options on the table at the moment."
"Our third option is to do a pincer attack to wipe out their forces, then march toward Tzarsbourgh."
"We can always push the reservists forward to fill the gap in the battle line."
"We don't even have enough reserves to fill potential weaknesses."
"All thanks to you. You were the one who pushed President Rayne to remove mandatory conscription."
"They are untrained soldiers with little experience. We cannot rely on them to hold the line for long."
"The expansion of our land forces will serve to fill any gap we have in our border."
"In any case, our soldiers in the main armies are well-drilled and prepared to carry out any strategy we choose."
"Unfortunately, we have to choose wisely. Our troops' combat readiness is at an all-time low. It will take them some time on the battlefield to regain their sharpness."
"Have we heard anything from our allies, yet?"
entradas.menu: "Have we heard anything from our allies, yet?"

entradas.text: "I'm ready to choose our first move."
entradas.menu: "I'm ready to choose our first move."

entradas.text: "Whichever strategy we choose, our major allies will cover our flaws. We don't have to worry about our army's weaknesses."
"More precisely, at strategic points on the path to Tzarsbourgh from Estord."
"More precisely, at strategic points on the path to Tzarsbourgh from Estord."
"If we choose to assault Tzarsbourgh, our first step will be to have our bombers strike them on the frontline."
"Then our tanks will come in and puncture their defense at Crimsrad, followed up by our soldiers."
"Then our tanks will come in and puncture their defense at Crimsrad, followed up by our soldiers."
"After we penetrate their line, we will race for Tzarsbourgh, threatening an encirclement of their forces."
"Which all sounds much easier than it is."
"Let me remind you that we are butting heads with an army far larger than ours."
"They can cover weaknesses in their line rapidly. Which will leave our troops that are pushing through isolated."
"You are forgetting that we will have the element of surprise."
"We should strike first when the enemy has yet to organize a proper defense."
"Their sky will be filled with Sordland's bombers and fighters. We will have air superiority."
"With our expanded air fleet, we can launch a carpet of bomb strikes on them."
"General Kruger, I want to remind that you were against modernizing our air force at first. Now you see its benefits."
"Our modernized airforce has the capacity to accurately strike at the strategic targets across the battlefield."
"I simply use the tools I have, Iosef. As any good general would."
"With what airforce? We'll be overwhelmed by Rumburg's planes the moment they take off."
"Without air superiority, our troops will have a tough time on the field."
"Do I have to remind you that even with our airforce expanded, Rumburg's fleet will still be equal to or larger than ours?"
"The Queen has ensured her royal submarines are under state secrecy. Thus, our intelligence officers are having a hard time spotting them."
"We will feint at an assault on Crimsrad, with the full intention of tricking the enemy."
"They are a police force, Valken. Their skills will certainly be of use during the war, but they shouldn't join the front line as common soldiers."
"The gendarmerie can be deployed on the mainline as well to support the war effort."
"Casualties are expected to a certain extent, so that Rumburg does not become suspicious of our real intentions. When they believe they are winning, they will push for Estord."

"With their confidence so high, they'll never expect the 2nd army from the east and the 6th army from the west which are holding their striking positions. At the moment they capture Estord, we'll pull the trigger."
"Our bombers will strike at the logistical hubs behind them. After which we will attack Estord from all three sides, destroying the enemy forces."
"Are you mad, General?! Letting Rumburg's invaders into Sordland?"
"Our modernized army is trained and equipped for such a task."
"I am confident that we will achieve complete victory with my strategy."
"Might as well invite the Queen to tea in Holsord while you're at it."
"Furthermore, our reservists are new soldiers. News of the initial defeat will damage their morale. Which might collapse our eastern front in Agnland."
"That is why I advised us to remove mandatory conscription."
"Can't we just let our troops know the attack is a distraction?"
entradas.menu: "Can't we just let our troops know the attack is a distraction?"

entradas.text: "Why don't we have the generals let them in on the strategy?"
entradas.menu: "Why don't we have the generals let them in on the strategy?"

entradas.text: "Maybe the defeat will raise the stakes for them. Inspire them to fight harder."
entradas.menu: "Maybe the defeat will raise the stakes for them. Inspire them to fight harder."

entradas.text: "And jeopardize the whole plan by having it leak to Rumburg's spies?"
"No, Mr. President, it is too risky."
"The gendarmerie will be of excellent help during our strike at Estord."
"They know every nook and cranny of the city."
"I share General Lancea's opinion that a direct attack on Tzarsbourgh is unwise."
"General Kruger, your confidence and bold strategy are commendable, but a blunt, by-the-book approach like this will only work if our forces are equal in power."
"I apologize for my incompetence, sir."
"However unreliable our allies can be, they can cover our military weaknesses. if we utilize our cooperation well."
"Doubling down on defense and grinding down the enemy's forces has some merit to it."
"Looking at the plans that have been proposed..."
"Iosef's pincer strategy seems to work well with what we have right now."
"I don't see a path to victory by ourselves."
"Let us dig down and invite them to certain death."
entradas.menu: "Let us dig down and invite them to certain death."

entradas.text: "We need to fight smarter if we are weaker. Let's go with Iosef's pincer plan."
entradas.menu: "We need to fight smarter if we are weaker. Let's go with Iosef's pincer plan."

entradas.text: "We will show them what we're made of. Let us march toward Tzarsbourgh."
entradas.menu: "We will show them what we're made of. Let us march toward Tzarsbourgh."

entradas.text: "So we're doomed, then."
"The decision is already made, Iosef."
"Excellent!"
"So we're doomed, then."
"The decision is already made, Valken."
"After all my explanations, this is the path you choose?"
"A rash decision, boy. One that could spell the end of Sordland."
"An excellent choice, Mr. President."
"I am lost for words."
"What have you decided about Wehlen?"
"On to our allies then."
"Have them reinforce our troops in the Nargis region."
entradas.menu: "Have them reinforce our troops in the Nargis region."

entradas.text: "Have them go through Lards and Merdon to flank the Rumburg army from the east."
entradas.menu: "Have them go through Lards and Merdon to flank the Rumburg army from the east."

entradas.text: "No, have them assist us in the pincer attack."
entradas.menu: "No, have them assist us in the pincer attack."

entradas.text: "Yes, I trust that they will be able to take Dome."
entradas.menu: "Yes, I trust that they will be able to take Dome."

entradas.text: "Meanwhile, Agnolia would be assaulting Dome, creating a second front."
"Lespia's armies will reinforce us on the front line."
"Should we ask Valgsland to assist us in Agnland?"
"Yes, we need to focus on that front."
entradas.menu: "Yes, we need to focus on that front."

entradas.text: "No, Their armies would be more useful drawing Rumburg away."
entradas.menu: "No, Their armies would be more useful drawing Rumburg away."

entradas.text: "I'll send them a message to do an amphibious landing north of Rumburg."
"That's the time for us to immediately launch a counter-offensive toward Tzarsbourgh and take the city."
"Excellent!"
"Excellent!"
"So. Let's assume that at this point, we have Tzarsbourgh in our hands."
"This is just the first step. From this point on, it will be harder since we're going deep into hostile territory."
"I see two options for us to move forward."
"We can continue pushing toward Thornbourgh and capture the queen."
"Or we turn our attention towards Dome."
"We risk being flanked from the east with either strategy but it is a risk we must take."
"How would we take Thornbourgh?"
entradas.menu: "How would we take Thornbourgh?"

entradas.text: "Why can't we just defend Tzarsbourgh from this point on?"
entradas.menu: "Why can't we just defend Tzarsbourgh from this point on?"

entradas.text: "Your opinion, Colonel?"
entradas.menu: "Your opinion, Colonel?"

entradas.text: "After Tzarsbourgh is taken, the enemy will be in shock and their morale will be low."

"However, if we hesitate for even a moment, this window will close. Even worse, the enemy will realize that we are overextending and will try to cut us off. This will leave the bulk of our army isolated in the cold north."
"Elaborate on the strategy around Dome."
entradas.menu: "Elaborate on the strategy around Dome."

entradas.text: "Fortunately, our modernized forces have been properly trained and prepared for exactly such a mission."
"Our gendarmerie can stay behind in Tzarsbourgh to cover our flank."
"As much as I want to crush all Rumburgian hope by taking their capital, our doctrine does not include these kinds of rapid advances."
"To boot, our supply line will be stretched too thin, creating a weak point that can be exploited by the enemy."
"We can deploy our reserve in Tzarsbourgh to help with the defense there."
"What about our allies?"
entradas.menu: "What about our allies?"

entradas.text: "If we choose to push toward Thornbourgh, it needs to be quick and decisive. It is unwise to take any of our allies with us."
"We can either have them stay and defend our flank in Tzarsbourgh or assault Dome."
"On that note, I would like to advise against having the Wehlen army fight together with our other allies."
"Especially Lespia, given their history of conflicts around immigration."
"It will leave us out in the open and susceptible to a Rumburg pincer attack."
"That is out of the question, Mr. President"
"They can strike us from all three directions, north, west, and, of course, east from Dome."
"It will leave us out in the open and susceptible to a Rumburg pincer attack."
"They can strike us from all three directions, north, west, and, of course, east from Dome."
"Dome and Tzarsbourgh are excellently linked logistically. There is a railway between the two cities."
"Just like the L-1 between Lachaven and Holsord."
"This will aid us in transporting military supplies and troops."
"With that said, control of the rail system is key because Rumburg can utilize it as well."
"Just like the L-1 between Lachaven and Holsord."
"This will aid us in transporting military supplies and troops."
"You are overestimating their capabilities, Iosef. Our vast armed forces will quickly overwhelm them."
"We can easily launch an assault on Dome within half a week after taking Tzarsbourgh."
"If they can withstand our assault, they can launch a counter-offensive with ease from the direction of Dome to retake Tzarsbourgh."
"We would lose everything we had gained so far."
"The gendarmerie can stay behind and protect our flank from Tzarsbourgh."
"The reservists can be deployed in Tzarsbourgh to help with the defenses."
"With Valgsland executing a naval invasion from the north, we can create another pincer movement, this time right at their capital."
"Otherwise the invasion from the north will still continue splitting Rumburg's attention and troops."
"Our industrial production and trade lanes will be crucial at that point in the war."
"With the strength of our navy, we will be able to stop Rumburg from raiding or blockading us in the Markian Sea."
"Our military industrial output is at the highest it's ever been. We won't have a problem providing our armed forces with what they need."
"Three cheers for the Sordish military industrial complex."
"Our military production is at an all-time low right now. We lack supplies in some units."
"I'm ready to decide."
entradas.menu: "I'm ready to decide."

entradas.text: "Without sufficient production capacity or supplies to be procured through trade, our chances at victory seem slim."
"What have you done to Sordland, Rayne?"
"Our chances certainly seem high. You've done well for our military, Rayne."
"Luckily, we have a defense in depth strategy thanks to our reinforcement armies. Whichever strategy we choose, we will have some room to manouver."
"Considering the size of our forces, taking Dome is the ideal course of action."
"We should push for Thornbourgh. Our modernized forces will serve this purpose best."
"With the current state sorry of our forces, it will be hard to succeed in either strategy on our own."
"Your decision, Mr. President."
"We will march toward Thornbourgh and end this war with a decisive strike against the enemy."
entradas.menu: "We will march toward Thornbourgh and end this war with a decisive strike against the enemy."

entradas.text: "We will attack Dome and lay out a defensive line. Let them come and get us."
entradas.menu: "We will attack Dome and lay out a defensive line. Let them come and get us."

entradas.text: "If by some luck we succeed, it would be too late to attack Thornbourgh from Dome."
"Rumburg would either reinforce their southern defenses or the Queen would come to her senses and flee the capital."
"Even if we manage to capture Thornbourgh later, we won't be able to hold it during the winter. Our supply lines will be too stretched out for that."
"However, with the capture of Dome, there will be no need to take Thornbourgh."
"It would be too late to attack anyway."
"Rumburg would either reinforce their southern defenses or the Queen would come to her senses and flee the capital."
"Even if we manage to capture Thornbourgh without their Queen, we won't be able to hold it during the winter. Our supply lines will be too stretched out for that."
"However, with two of their largest cities under our control, we can lay out a defensive line and force Rumburg to capitulate, since their economy would slowly crumble afterwards."
"However, with two of their largest cities in our hand, we can lay out a defensive line."
"It is decided then."
"It is decided then."
"You are wasting an opportunity to end this war once and for all, Mr. President."
"I'm warning you, if Rumburg listens to their well-trained officers, this plan will not work."
"It is decided, Iosef."
"I'm adding it to our battle plan."
"Now, let us decide on our allies' movements during this phase."
"What should the Wehlen army do?"
"Have them attack Dome."
entradas.menu: "Have them attack Dome."

entradas.text: "Have them stay in Tzarsbourgh to cover our back."
entradas.menu: "Have them stay in Tzarsbourgh to cover our back."

entradas.text: "What about Lespia's armies?"
"Lespia's impressive army will do well in guarding our flanks. That should be their positioning."
entradas.menu: "Lespia's impressive army will do well in guarding our flanks. That should be their positioning."

entradas.text: "Lespia can surely take Dome within a week. Let's coordinate with them on that."
entradas.menu: "Lespia can surely take Dome within a week. Let's coordinate with them on that."

entradas.text: "Agnolia will probably try to assault Dome after they have finished assisting us in the pincer attack."
"Agnolia will probably still be struggling to take Dome at this point."
"At this point, Valgsland will already have created a foothold at the north-eastern coast of Rumburg."
"Since the Valgsland army would be poised to act, where should we send them next?"
"Valgsland can surely take Dome within a week."
entradas.menu: "Valgsland can surely take Dome within a week."

entradas.text: "Let's have them guard our flanks."
entradas.menu: "Let's have them guard our flanks."

entradas.text: "And that, gentlemen, is our plan against Rumburg."
Iosef handed me the order and waited for me to sign the document.
Its title was "Operation Fallen Crown".
I signed off on Operation Fallen Crown.
entradas.menu: Sign off on it.

entradas.text: He turned to the generals in the room.
The generals saluted and the War Room dispersed to begin the preparations.
Valken turned to the generals in the room.
"That makes it official, then."
"We have work to do. Get back to your posts immediately."
"We have work to do. Get back to your posts immediately."
"Mr. President. We will need your executive order to mobilize the forces."
"We only have one chance at victory."
"If we falter at any point during this war, it will be the end of Sordland as we know it."
Only three people were left in the room. Me, Deivid and the Colonel.
Only two people were left in the room. Me and Deivid.
Only two people were left in the room. Me and Colonel Soll.
Deivid approached me.
"Win or lose, this will be my last great contribution to my country."
"Let's protect our Republic, Anton."
"That is our job, and we will succeed."
entradas.menu: "That is our job, and we will succeed."

entradas.text: "For our Republic."
entradas.menu: "For our Republic."

entradas.text: "I will continue to do so until my last breath, Deivid."
entradas.menu: "I will continue to do so until my last breath, Deivid."

entradas.text: Deivid gave me a tired smile.
He warmly shook my hand before moving toward the door.
The Colonel and I turned to face each other.
"Thank you, Colonel. For being here."
entradas.menu: "Thank you, Colonel. For being here."

entradas.text: "When will you trust me to lead on my own, Colonel?"
entradas.menu: "When will you trust me to lead on my own, Colonel?"

entradas.text: "Well? Did I make you proud?"
entradas.menu: "Well? Did I make you proud?"

entradas.text: "Where else would I be? A good leader is always there for his country in times of need."
"Trust must be earned, Anton. But the crucible of war may make a leader out of you yet."
"Let's hope that the next time we meet, it will be under a Sordish Flag in Tzarsbourgh."
"Rest assured, it will be."
entradas.menu: "Rest assured, it will be."

entradas.text: "Ha. When we win, I will personally invite you to supper in Thornbourgh."
entradas.menu: "Ha. When we win, I will personally invite you to supper in Thornbourgh."

entradas.text: "God willing."
entradas.menu: "God willing."

entradas.text: Soll saluted me and then headed for the door.
I stood there alone in the war room, looking at the map of Sordland laid out on the table. I picked up one of the little metal tokens on it and turned it over in my hand.
"Our planes will bomb them to smithereens!"
"Any questions, Mr. President?"

"But we have to consider the defenses in and around the city of Dome. Ever since they took it from Agnolia, they have been building up fortifications in case of an Agnolian attempt at retaking the city."
"Furthermore, due to the length of the operation to take Tzarsbourgh, they would come to the realization that Dome is our next target."
"There is no guarantee that we can take a well-reinforced and fortified city while holding the line at the western and the northern fronts."
"Especially around Dome. They took it from Agnolia because of the oil fields surrounding it. Their industrial sector has since heavily relied on them."
"With their oil supply cut, they won't have the fuel for their huge war machine and their economy will slowly collapse. We will be effectively choking them until they capitulate."
"Also, we can deploy our reserve in Tzarsbourgh to help with the defense there."
"What is your decision on the first phase, Mr. President?"
"Though our armed forces have been reduced in size, they are all well equipped for the war. "
"Unfortunately, our armed forces are under-equipped. Not all soldiers will have a grenade or handgun, but at least we will have manpower."
"The estimates put their active military personnel at around 900,000 to one million. Meanwhile, we have approximately 400,000 soldiers on the ground."
"The estimates put their active military personnel at around 900,000 to one million. Meanwhile, we have approximately 200,000 soldiers on the ground."
"The estimates put their active military personnel at around 900.000 to one million. Meanwhile, we have approximately 350,000 soldiers on the ground."
"The estimates put their active military personnel at around 900,000 to one million. Meanwhile, we have approximately 150,000 soldiers on the ground."
"The estimates put their active military personnel at around 900.000 to one million. Meanwhile, we have approximately 100,000 soldiers on the ground."
"The estimates put their active military personnel at around 900.000 to one million. Meanwhile, we have approximately 300,000 soldiers on the ground."
"As for their airforce, our estimates put the number of aircraft in their fleet at around 700."
"While Rumburg is recovering from its losses, Tzarsbourgh will be ripe for the taking."
"You're right...We will make do somehow."
Iosef's shoulders dropped in defeat.
"When they launch their initial offensive, our soldiers and tanks will be entrenched in strategic and well-fortified positions."
"Let them throw their manpower at our impenetrable line of defense."
"With their pride shattered, their morale low, and their line disorganized, we will launch an all-out assault to strike the finishing blow."
"We will grind down their armies that they are so proud of."
Iosef and I signed the plan documents for the first phase of the war and handed them off to the nearest soldier.
"The gendarmerie and the reservists can stay behind and protect our flank from Tzarsbourgh."
"Very well. I will add it to our battle plan."
"But you are the commander-in-chief. I will not question your decision."
"I had a feeling my guidance might be needed."
Iosef paused for a moment before picking his pointer back up.
An assistant scrambled to find him a chair. He put aside his cane and sat at the head of the table while the rest of the room stood rigidly at attention.
"At ease, everyone."
"We can only hope."
"We shall see."
It represented thousands of men who were willing to die for this country. For me.
Including my own son.
I hoped I would not let them down.
"Hence opening up a brief window of opportunity for us to march toward Thornbourgh."
"There is still animosity between Bergia's Bludish population and the Wehzek soldiers."
"However, it won't be a problem if we make a public statement about the dire situation of Sordland."
"Thank goodness you've got those traitors under control."
"Knowing Smolak, he might just abandon us as soon as the situation gets difficult."
"He wouldn't dare."
entradas.menu: "He wouldn't dare."

entradas.text: "After everything I've done for him? Never."
entradas.menu: "After everything I've done for him? Never."

entradas.text: "One thing at a time, Mr. President."
"It would also deter Valgsland from attempting an invasion. Allowing Agnolia to completely focus on the north."
"With their navy patrolling in the Markian Sea, we can enjoy their protection from any Rumburg naval attacks."
"We can have them reinforce our troops in the Nargis region..."
"Or we can have them flank the main Rumburg force by going through Lards and Merdon."
"However, since we have Bergia under the central government now, it won't be a problem."
"The generals of Wehlen established a communication line with the Sordish Armed Forces, pledging support in the war."
"Either way, they will have to move through Bergia to reach the front quickly."
"Honestly, I won't be surprised if Rumburg overwhelms them at the Dome frontline."
"The chancellor of Valgsland has sent us his regards."
"Their massive army has to move to the frontline."
"Unfortunately, they are too far away to arrive in time for the first wave."
"He'll face the full might of Sordland if he dares to do that."
entradas.menu: "He'll face the full might of Sordland if he dares to do that."

entradas.text: "You should have gotten those traitors under control when you had the chance, Rayne. They'll tear the Wehzeks to pieces at the first opportunity."
"Prime Minister Van Hoorten contacted us and said that his war target is Dome."
"Unfortunately, their chances of success are very low."
"Unfortunately, they are too far away to arrive in time for the first wave."
"Since our navy isn't strong enough to assure them security, the Agnolians will be worried about Valgsland seizing the chance to invade Heljiland."
"Their massive army has to move to the frontline."
"Prime Minister Alvarez is a very opportunistic person."
"We could use it to transport Lespia's massive armies to the border in time for the first wave."
"I'm afraid that he might withdraw his soldiers if we suffer a defeat in our opening battles."
"With the strength of their military force, they will probably take Dome by themselves."
entradas.menu: "With the strength of their military force, they will probably take Dome by themselves."

entradas.text: "President Smolak has contacted us and promised assistance in this war."
"This will create a new front away from their southern deployments, drawing the pressure away from our front. And if a few communists get killed in the process, so be it."
"However, our recognition of the Hejiland Island and our impressive navy could alleviate the Agnolian troop positioning there."
"However, our recognition of the Hejiland Island and our impressive navy could alleviate the Agnolian troop positioning there."
"Since the situation is quite hostile, the Wehlen armies might have a difficult time moving through the region."
"If our navy is not prepared to deter Agnolia from retaking the island, Valgsland might pull their troops back."
"However, the Heljiland island is still a problem for them."
"We can ask them to transport their marine army to support us on our front."
"This will create a new front away from their southern deployments, drawing the pressure away from our front."
"However, their massive navy enables interesting strategic options."
"Can they take Dome back on their own?"
entradas.menu: "Can they take Dome back on their own?"

entradas.text: "I don't trust the soldiers from Wehlen. Their troops are disorganized and undisciplined."
"Another strategy to entertain is to have them launch an amphibious landing of their army on Rumburg's eastern coast."
"Another strategy to entertain is to have them launch an amphibious landing of their army on Rumburg's eastern coast."
"I have my own doubts about the Malenyevists' commitment to the war."
"Unfortunately, their chances of success are very low."
"That is why we managed to defeat them in the past. Our will was stronger than theirs."
"It would also deter Valgsland from attempting an invasion. Allowing Agnolia to completely focus on the north."
"Agnolia will join us in the war."
"Since we haven't recognized Heljiland, the Agnolians are more worried than ever about Valgsland invading."
"The generals of Wehlen established a communication line with the Sordish Armed Forces, pledging support in the war."
"We can also ask them to join us in the pincer strategy."
"Rumburg took Dome in the past. It is only natural that they want their ancestral homeland back now."
"The constructed L-1 railway will be very helpful in our push north."
"Unfortunately, their chances of success are very low."
"Nonetheless, it's undoubtable that their troops will be able to make up for any of our own army's weaknesses."
"Judging from the past and the imperialistic nature of the southerners... I wouldn't be surprised if they refuse to leave after the war."
"However, if that is the case, they won't be present during the first wave of the attack on Rumburg."
"The constructed L-1 railway will be very helpful in our push north."
"Rumburg took Dome in the past. It is only natural that they want their ancestral homeland back now."
"Rumburg took Dome in the past. It is only natural that they want their ancestral homeland back now."
"The Agnolians will likely leave half of their army defending that goddamn island."
"That might be a problem. If Rumburg shatters the Agnolian army, they will have access to Agnland and they can flank us from the east."
"With their navy patrolling in the Markian Sea, we can enjoy their protection from any Rumburg naval attacks."
"Honestly, I won't be surprised if Rumburg overwhelms them at the Dome frontline."
"We could use it to transport Lespia's massive armies to the border in time for the first wave."
"They will only field two armored and mechanized armies with no more than 20 divisions."
"Prime Minister Alvarez has already announced support for the war."
"However, that would leave Agnolia vulnerable from a direct attack from Dome, leaving their capital within striking distance of Rumburg."
"If our navy is not prepared to deter Agnolia from retaking the island, Valgsland might pull their troops back."
"However, the Heljiland island is still a problem for them."
"Unfortunately, their chances of success are very low."
"This will create a new front away from their southern deployments, drawing the pressure away from our front. And if a few commies get killed in the process, so be it."
"However, we are still vulnerable to Rumburg's navy, especially their submarines. Let's hope our own naval forces are up for the task of protecting the sea lanes."
"Another strategy to entertain is to have them launch an amphibious landing of their army at the eastern coast of Rumburg."
"We can ask them to transport their marine army to support us on our front."
"However, their massive navy enables interesting strategic options."
"I have my own doubts about the Malenyevists' commitment to the war."
"I doubt they can take back Dome on their own."
entradas.menu: "I doubt they can take back Dome on their own."

entradas.text: "Judging from the past and the imperialistic nature of the southerners... I wouldn't be surprised if they refuse to leave after the war."
"They will need to concentrate their troops if they are to hold out against Rumburg's superior forces."
"However, if that is the case, they won't be present during the first wave of the attack on Rumburg."

"This will surely make us the enemy of the Queen but if we triumph, she won't be matter enough for us to worry about."

"Prime Minister Alvarez is a very opportunistic person."
"I was afraid that he might withdraw his soldiers if we suffer a defeat in our opening battles."
"But with his army arriving on the frontline with us, this is unlikely to happen."

"We can also secure necessary supplies via trade. Nations within OMEC have began to send us war supplies and laying down sanctions toward Rumburg. However, We will need to make sure the Markian Sea is under our naval control during the war."
"Unfortunately, our trade volume is not enough to support our war effort. We will have to rely on our own production."
"They even send their prestigious airforce which add 60 air wings to aid us in maintaining air superiority."
"I suspect this is thanks to our country's economy entering a great recovery period."
"I suspect this is thanks to our economic direction which is fitting with Lespia's model."
"With the state of our economy, we will soon be the shining jewel in Merkopa. As such worth a larger investment from Prime Minister Alvarez's point of view."
"Though the state of our economy is not great, Prime Minister Alvarez sees us as a potential trade partner. As such worth a larger investment from his point of view."
"I suspect this is due to the state of our economy. Prime Minister Alvarez might have judged us as a bad investment."
"However, they refused to move their airforce to help us in the war. As they said that they need to 'defend their other interests'. "
"I am not surprised, to be honest. With our economy doing into a depression, we do not worth that much from Prime Minister Alvarez's point of view."
"Which sounds like a load of crab to me."
"Lespia's military is truly impressive in terms of both size and technology. They field two fully armored and mechanized armies with more than 40 divisions."
"Lespia's military is truly impressive in terms of both size and technology. They field two fully armored and mechanized armies with more than 40 divisions."
"And they even refused to move their airforce to help us in the war. As they said that they need to 'defend their other interests'. "
"So he only sent only a portion of his army as a gesture of the alliance knowing full well that they might die !?."
"What a heartless capitalist bastard!."
Iosef took a deep breath to calm himself.
"Iosef, calm yourself. We must not lose our heads during this critical moment."
"Iosef, calm yourself. We must not lose our heads during this critical moment."
"Iosef, calm yourself. We must not lose our heads during this critical moment."
"Having said that, with Lespia's airforce at our disposal, this won't be a problem."
"Having said that, with Lespia's airforce at our disposal, this won't be a problem."
"We can also secure necessary supplies via trade. We need to make sure the Markian Sea is under our naval control during the war."
"Not to mention effort and time needed to reorganize and execute such attack due to the size of our army."
"However, Agnolia's persistence in attacking Dome with or without us brought up some dilemmas."
"They are even requesting more supplies for their siege of Dome."
"Unfortunately, we barely have enough supplies for ourselves so that is out of the question."
"With our production capacity and trade volume, we will just have enough supplies to support them."
"Thanks to the H3-Highway in Agnland, we won't have much logistical problems in transferring supplies to Agnolia's front."

"However, we do have some problems in how we transfer our supplies to the frontline. Agnland's infrastructure is in a sorry state so it will not be possible to ship large volumes of supplies to Agnolia's front line in time."
"Tzarsbourgh will be surrounded from all north, west, and east. We will be practically a sitting duck at that point."
"If Rumburg armies manage to launch a counter-attack through Agnolia from Dome due to Agnolia failing in taking the city, we will be in big trouble."
"It's all good if they managed to accomplish retaking the city but I and our generals don't think that they can."
"We have to think carefully about which strategy we choose here. Without any reserve to cover our back, one wrong move and we will lose everything."
"You're afraid that Maartin might backstab us?"
entradas.menu: "You're afraid that Maartin might backstab us?"

entradas.text: "No, he wouldn't dare. The international repercussions would be far too high."
"First you beg me to call Agnolia in, now you're suspicious of them?"
entradas.menu: "First you beg me to call Agnolia in, now you're suspicious of them?"

entradas.text: "Don't get me wrong, Mr. President. The point I made still stands."
"First you beg me to call Lespia in, now you're suspicious of them?"
entradas.menu: "First you beg me to call Lespia in, now you're suspicious of them?"

entradas.text: "First you beg me to call Valgsland in, now you're suspicious of them?"
entradas.menu: "First you beg me to call Valgsland in, now you're suspicious of them?"

entradas.text: "First you beg me to call Wehlen in, now you're suspicious of them?"
entradas.menu: "First you beg me to call Wehlen in, now you're suspicious of them?"

entradas.text: "You're afraid that Alvarez might backstab us?"
entradas.menu: "You're afraid that Alvarez might backstab us?"

entradas.text: "You're afraid that Hegel might backstab us?"
entradas.menu: "You're afraid that Hegel might backstab us?"

entradas.text: "You're afraid that Smolak might backstab us?"
entradas.menu: "You're afraid that Smolak might backstab us?"

entradas.text: Deivid gracefully motioned for Iosef to step aside. He was now at the head of the table.
"I'm sure that he will agree to fight by our side."
"However, depending on our plans and our past interactions with him, his commitment to the war may change."
"Unfortunately, Agnland and Nargis will be mostly shut down due to the war happening at the border."
"Most businesses have already begun to flee the city of Lachaven, which is our primary trade hub. Thus our economy will take a big hit due to this fact."
I heard the sound of boots running down the hall. A soldier rushed in, urgently pulled Iosef aside and whispered in his ear.
The general's face turned white. He hurriedly ran a hand over the medals on his uniform.
"Mr. President, it seems we will be joined by a very esteemed guest today."
"Who is it?"
entradas.menu: "Who is it?"

entradas.text: "Another general? I thought everyone was here."
entradas.menu: "Another general? I thought everyone was here."

entradas.text: "Must be someone important to make you react like that."
entradas.menu: "Must be someone important to make you react like that."

entradas.text: "If you tell me you've brought Valken Kruger back, I will fire you on the spot."
entradas.menu: "If you tell me you've brought Valken Kruger back, I will fire you on the spot."

entradas.text: Before he could answer, the door swung open. Every single man in the room immediately stood bolt upright and saluted.
"Colonel."
"Mr. President is joking. We all appreciate your attendance."
"I don't think the Colonel's war credentials need to be reiterated."
"Having him here will be of immense help to us. As well as a morale booster for our troops."
"I seem to remember you pleading for my aid, Mr. President. You can't get rid of me as easily as you got rid of General Kruger."
"Thank you for accepting my invitation."
entradas.menu: "Thank you for accepting my invitation."

entradas.text: "And thank you for extending it. You have shown great leadership in times of peace. Let us see how you act in times of war."
"Whatever differences I have with you, Rayne, I would rather Sordland remain under your leadership than fall to those bastard Rums."
"I would suggest that we refrain from attacking Tzarsbourgh directly."
"It's the sort of blunt, by-the-book approach General Kruger might have favored, but it will only work if our forces are equal in power."
